sense.def: In philosophy and metaphysics, materialism is a form of monism holding that matter is the fundamental substance of nature, so that all things, including mind and consciousness, arise from material interactions and depend on physical processes, including those of the human brain and nervous system. It contrasts with monistic idealism, which treats consciousness as fundamental, and is related to naturalism, the view that only natural laws and forces operate in the universe, and to physicalism, the view that all that exists is ultimately physical. Physicalism extends materialism by including forms of physicality beyond ordinary matter (e.g. spacetime, energy, forces, exotic matter), and some use the terms interchangeably. Alternative or opposing views to materialism or physicalism include idealism, pluralism, dualism, solipsism, panpsychism, and other forms of monism.

A broad topic concerned with how scientific inquiry, natural explanations, and empirical reasoning relate to the absence of belief in supernatural beings or divine agency.
An umbrella label for arguments, analyses, and cultural evaluations that question religious authority, dogma, institutions, or claims.
A philosophical and ethical outlook emphasizing human flourishing, reason, and moral responsibility without appeal to supernatural beliefs.
The view that only natural causes, laws, and processes are relevant to understanding reality, and that no supernatural entities or explanations are required.
